summary: View CSAF Summary Hitachi Energy is aware of OS command injection and Dirty Frag vulnerabilities that affect CoreTec product versions listed in this document. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could result in impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. title: Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience
summary: CISA, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre), and partners are releasing joint guidance, Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience , to help organizations understand and manage token usage in support of operations. As organizations adopt third-party super intelligence (SI) services, token-based usage models can affect cost, performance, and access to critical services. Unmanaged token consumption may contribute to rising and unpredictable costs, reduced service availability, degraded performance, token exhaustion, and denial-of-tokens or denial-of-wallet attacks. The guidance outlines practical steps organizations can take to prioritize token allocation, design efficient workflows, improve user prompting practices, leverage caching and reusable context, optimize data before submission, and monitor token consumption over time. Critical infrastructure owners and operators can use this guidance to identify mission-critical functions that depend on SI, understand service provider and operational dependencies, and plan for reduced SI availability during outages, incidents, or periods of high demand. Cyber defenders can also use the guidance to manage SI-enabled cyber defense workflows while maintaining human oversight, governance, and strong cybersecurity fundamentals.

title: AL26-028 – Campagne continue d’hameçonnage vocal lié au soutien technique ciblant des organisations canadiennes
summary: Numéro : AL26-028 Date : 28 octobre 2026 Auditoire La présente alerte s’adresse aux professionnelles et professionnels des TI et aux gestionnaires. Objet Une alerte vise à sensibiliser les destinataires à une cybermenace récemment relevée pouvant toucher les biens d’information électroniques et à fournir des conseils supplémentaires en matière de détection et d’atténuation. Le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité (ou Centre pour la cybersécurité) peut offrir une assistance supplémentaire aux destinataires qui en font la demande. Détails Le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité (Centre pour la cybersécurité) est au courant d’une campagne continue d’hameçonnage vocal ciblant des organisations canadiennes, notamment dans le secteur juridique et judiciaire et dans le secteur des finances. Plusieurs entreprises canadiennes ont été ciblées par des personnes qui se font passer pour du personnel de soutien technique interne et qui dirigent les employées ou employés vers des pages d’ouverture de session frauduleuses. L’infrastructure et le savoir-faire utilisés correspondent à des activités menées par un auteur de menace motivé par l’appât du gain ayant fait l’objet de rapports publics Note de bas de page 1 Note de bas de page 2 . Tout au long de 2026, ces activités sont passées d’un secteur à l’autre et ciblent de plus en plus des organisations du secteur juridique et judiciaire et du secteur des finances depuis juillet Note de bas de page 1 . Le Centre pour la cybersécurité a identifié des infrastructures connexes où figurait le nom d’organisations canadiennes remontant au mois de janvier. Les activités recensées en octobre ciblaient principalement le secteur juridique et judiciaire. La campagne réussit à contourner l’authentification multifacteur (AMF) grâce à un relais en temps réel et change fréquemment les domaines utilisés comme leurres, ce qui réduit l’efficacité des listes de rejet. title: AL26-028 – Ongoing Help Desk Voice Phishing Campaign Targeting Canadian Organizations
summary: Serial number: AV26-028 Date: October 28, 2026 Audience This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers. Purpose An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested. Details The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of an ongoing voice phishing (vishing) campaign targeting Canadian organizations, including organizations in the legal and financial sectors. Multiple Canadian firms have been targeted by individuals impersonating internal IT support and directing employees to fraudulent sign-in pages. The tradecraft and infrastructure are consistent with publicly reported operations by a financially motivated threat actor Footnote 1 Footnote 2 . Throughout 2026, this activity has shifted across sectors, increasingly targeting finance and legal organizations since July Footnote 1 . The Cyber Centre has identified related infrastructure naming Canadian organizations since January, with October activity concentrated on the legal sector. The campaign bypasses conventional multi-factor authentication (MFA) through real-time relay and frequently rotates lure domains, limiting the effectiveness of blocklists. Initial Access Help desk voice phishing: Callers impersonate internal IT or help desk staff and claim an urgent passkey migration, MFA enrolment or password change is required. Calls may target personal mobile phones, office phones or Microsoft Teams, and may spoof legitimate help desk numbers. Callers may reference internal IT staff or missed deadlines to add credibility and may end the call if the employee attempts independent verification Footnote 1 . title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
summary: On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. Public reports indicated that these vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution (RCE). The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Both vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities. [New] On 23 October, PHP disclosed a new RCE vulnerability. However, it affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk. PHP will not issue an out-of-band release for this vulnerability. Instead, organisations are advised to apply mitigation to fully protect from this RCE vector. CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.

title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
summary: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-88779 Citrix NetScaler Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.
